title: watched file is duplicated in callback in certain cases
description:
I have encountered an interesting case where watcher is sometimes firing the callback and reporting the same file has been changed more than once. Is this intended behaviour? I think this occurs when a file changes more than once before R is able to fire the callback. An example:

```
tf <- "/tmp/test"

w <- watcher::watcher(
  tf,
  \(file) {
    cat(
      "length:", length(file), "\n"
    )
  }
)

w$start()
```

then, in a separate terminal, if I run

```
echo 1 >> /tmp/test
```

Watcher reports "length: 1".

if I run

```
echo 2 >> /tmp/test; echo 3 >> /tmp/test
```

Watcher now reports "length: 2".

This has caused me issues because I was watching a json file, and essentially having a callback which ran `jsonlite::read_json(file)`, this leads to `file` erroring with `invalid 'description' argument` error. my solution is to simply take the first item for `file`, which is fine for my particular use case.

title: High CPU usage
description:
I tested the package on a windows 10 machine with Intel Core i5-13400T. 
During these tests I noticed that the CPU usage was quite high, even when applied to a relatively small folder.
When having two instances of `watcher` I noticed that CPU usage was ~50%.

Not sure if there is anything that could be done within the package and maybe it is directly linked to `ReadDirectoryChangesW`?
I originally planned to have a few instances running, which might lead to problems (e.g. 4 instances uses almost all of my CPU).

No idea if it is helpful but the function recurse into a directory, could it help to have an option to not watch recursively?

title: Allow use of 'libfswatch' in non-standard filesystem location
Determine type of file action
description:
Thanks for this great package! I have previously used powershell (`FileSystemWatcher`), however this package works much easier. The powershell solution I used before did however have the option to perform different actions based on the type of change. For instance a different function can be called in case a file is changed, created, deleted or renamed.
I was wondering if something similar could be achieved with this package as well?  I can find out what happened manually, based on the name of the file. But would be nice if there is a more elegant solution.

title: [feature request] Add `pattern` argument to `watcher`
description:
It would be nice for `watcher` to have a `pattern` argument so that one could (for example), just monitor `.log` files or `.html` files within a folder.

I looked at the source, but its all R6 and c++ so I don't think I can offer a PR for the feature unfortunately.

This is possibly somewhat related to [issue 14](https://github.com/r-lib/watcher/issues/14).

title: Multiple paths supplied to watcher
description:
`watcher` accepts a vector of paths for the `path` argument without error, but does not seem to monitor them:

```r
test <- watcher::watcher(path = c(here::here("DESCRIPTION"), here::here("LICENSE")))
test$start()
test$is_running()
[1] TRUE
test$get_path()
[1] "/xxx/DESCRIPTION"
[2] "/xxx/LICENSE" 
# change `here::here("DESCRIPTION")`
0: /xxx/DESCRIPTION
# change `here::here("LICENSE")`
# No output to stdout
```

Either it should accept multiple paths (that would be ideal), or it should give an error if multiple paths are given.

title: inotify_rm_watch: Invalid argument
description:
Under Linux, `inotify_rm_watch: Invalid argument` is output to stderr when the Watcher object is removed and garbage collected, i.e. when the finalizer is run.

Same as https://github.com/emcrisostomo/fswatch/issues/206.
